justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modestly upward-drifting baseline from what I assumed was a current price near 292–293. At the one-day horizon, I anchored closely to the prevailing level, expecting minimal drift given typical daily volatility in equity or commodity markets and the absence of any imminent scheduled catalysts. For the one-week estimate, I nudged the figure slightly higher to 295, reflecting a mild positive drift assumption consistent with a modest bullish bias in the underlying trend without strong mean-reversion pressure. The one-month estimate of 298 extends that gentle drift further, essentially assuming that the prevailing trend continues at a slow pace while acknowledging that monthly moves tend to revert somewhat toward medium-term averages.

The confidence interval widths were calibrated to typical realized volatility at each time horizon. Daily volatility on most liquid instruments tends to run in the range of 0.5–1.5% for a single session, which translated into the roughly ±9–10 point band at one day. At one week, I widened the interval to account for compounding uncertainty across five sessions and the possibility of intraweek macro announcements or sentiment shifts. The one-month interval is the widest because a full calendar month introduces exposure to central bank decisions, earnings releases, geopolitical developments, and broader macroeconomic data revisions, all of which can compound directional moves significantly.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside my stated intervals. On the downside, a surprise deterioration in macroeconomic data — such as a sharper-than-expected contraction in manufacturing activity or a stress event in credit markets — could easily breach the lower bound, particularly at the one-month horizon. A sudden risk-off episode driven by geopolitical escalation or a central bank policy surprise could also produce outsized moves. On the upside, a stronger-than-expected economic print, an unexpectedly dovish pivot from a major central bank, or a resolution of an ongoing geopolitical uncertainty could push prices well above 332 within a month. Liquidity conditions and positioning extremes are also worth noting — if the market is heavily one-sided, a squeeze in either direction could amplify moves beyond what historical volatility alone would suggest.
